results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Required] [Step]: Fetch page content using FIRECRAWL_SCRAPE (default to readable text/markdown; request HTML only when you must inspect raw tags/source).
[Required] [Step]: Validate the FIRECRAWL_SCRAPE result using returned metadata and non-empty content (don’t trust a success wrapper if the payload is empty or an error).
[Optional (if verifying crawl/indexing configuration)] [Step]: Fetch site policy and index-descriptor endpoints using FIRECRAWL_SCRAPE (run in parallel with the main page to confirm discoverability).
[Optional (if the page is client-rendered or needs interaction)] [Step]: Navigate/render using FIRECRAWL_START_AGENT, then re-run FIRECRAWL_SCRAPE on the resulting state/URL.
[Optional (if you need additional pages beyond the starting URL)] [Prerequisite]: Discover candidate URLs using FIRECRAWL_MAP_MULTIPLE_URLS_BASED_ON_OPTIONS (keep a short list to scrape).
[Optional (if scraping many known/discovered URLs)] [Step]: Scrape the URL list in bulk using FIRECRAWL_BATCH_SCRAPE (reduce per-URL calls).
[Optional (if FIRECRAWL_BATCH_SCRAPE is used)] [Next Step]: Retrieve completed results using FIRECRAWL_BATCH_SCRAPE_GET (retry/poll until ready).
[Optional (if you need structured fields rather than raw text)] [Next Step]: Convert scraped content into JSON using FIRECRAWL_EXTRACT (e.g., title, description, links, images).
[Fallback (if FIRECRAWL_SCRAPE output is empty or unusable)] [Fallback]: Re-scrape the same URL using SUPADATA_GET_WEB_SCRAPE to cross-check accessibility/content.
known_pitfalls: [FIRECRAWL_SCRAPE] Response content may be nested (commonly under response.data.data); assuming top-level markdown/html fields can cause missing-data errors.
[FIRECRAWL_SCRAPE] Can fail with "No active connection found for toolkit(s) 'firecrawl'" even for public pages.
[FIRECRAWL_SCRAPE] May emit throttling warnings under concurrency limits; a warning can still accompany a usable payload.
[FIRECRAWL_BATCH_SCRAPE_GET] Batch jobs are asynchronous; results may be unavailable immediately after FIRECRAWL_BATCH_SCRAPE.
[SUPADATA_GET_WEB_SCRAPE] May return empty content even when the page is accessible; treat as a cross-check, and it also requires an active supadata connection.

FIRECRAWL_SCRAPE.description: Scrapes a publicly accessible URL, optionally performing pre-scrape browser actions or extracting structured JSON using an LLM, to retrieve content in specified formats.

url.description: The fully qualified URL of the web page to scrape. Must start with 'http://' or 'https://' and be a valid web URL.

key.description: Key to press (e.g., 'Enter', 'Escape', 'Tab'), used with 'press' actions.

text.description: Text to be typed into an element, used with 'write' actions.

type.description: The type of browser action to perform on the page before scraping. Supported actions: 'wait', 'click', 'screenshot', 'write', 'press', 'scroll'.

selector.description: CSS selector for the HTML element targeted by the action. Required for actions like 'click' or 'write'.

milliseconds.description: Specifies a duration in milliseconds, e.g., for a 'wait' action or a delay.

items.description: Action to perform on the page

actions.description: An optional list of browser actions (e.g., click, write, wait, press) to perform on the page before scraping. Useful for interacting with dynamic content, filling forms, or navigating through page elements.

formats.description: A list of desired output formats for the scraped content. Defaults to ['markdown']. Cannot include both 'screenshot' and 'screenshot@fullPage'. If 'json' is included, jsonOptions must be provided.

timeout.description: Maximum time in milliseconds to wait for the scraping request to complete. Defaults to 30000.

waitFor.description: Time in milliseconds to wait for the page to load or for dynamic content to render before starting the scrape. Defaults to 0.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code to make the request from (e.g., 'US', 'AU', 'DE', 'JP').

languages.description: List of preferred languages and locales for the request, in order of priority. Uses format like 'en-US'.

excludeTags.description: A list of HTML tags to specifically exclude from the output. Content within these tags will be removed.

includeTags.description: A list of HTML tags to specifically include in the output. Content within these tags will be prioritized.

examples: Extract the main headline and the first paragraph.
What are the product specifications mentioned on this page?
Summarize the article in three bullet points.
prompt.description: A user-defined prompt for data extraction when a specific JSON schema is not provided. Guides the LLM on what information to extract.

schema.description: A JSON Schema object defining the structure for data extraction. The LLM will populate this schema with data from the page. The API requires 'type': 'object' at the root level. Supported formats: (1) Object schema with properties - used as-is. (2) Array schema with items - automatically wrapped as {type: object, properties: {items: <your_array_schema>}}; the extracted data will be returned under the 'items' key. (3) Simplified property definitions - automatically wrapped with type: object.

examples: Focus on product details and specifications.
systemPrompt.description: A system-level prompt to guide the LLM during JSON extraction, setting context or desired behavior. Note: This parameter is only supported in v1 API; it is ignored when using v2 API.

onlyMainContent.description: If true, attempts to extract only the main article content, excluding headers, footers, navigation bars, and ads. Defaults to true.

FIRECRAWL_START_AGENT.description: Tool to start an agent job for agentic web extraction with multi-page navigation and interaction capabilities. Use when you need to autonomously gather data from the web with complex navigation requirements. The agent can search, navigate, and extract information across multiple pages based on your natural language prompt.

urls.description: Specific URLs to constrain the agent's search. If provided, the agent will start from these URLs. If not provided, the agent will autonomously search the web.

examples: Get the latest news about AI
Find all job openings at Y Combinator companies
Extract pricing information from SaaS product pages
prompt.description: Natural language description of what data you want to extract. The agent will autonomously navigate and interact with web pages to gather this information.

schema.description: JSON schema defining the structure of data you want returned. Must be a valid JSON Schema object with properties and types. This ensures the extracted data matches your desired format.

maxCredits.description: Maximum credits to spend on the request. The agent will stop when this limit is reached, preventing unexpected costs. If not specified, the agent will continue until the task is complete.

strictConstrainToURLs.description: Whether to strictly limit the agent to only the provided URLs. If true, the agent will not navigate to external links. If false or not specified, the agent can follow links to gather more information.

FIRECRAWL_MAP_MULTIPLE_URLS_BASED_ON_OPT.description: Maps a website by discovering URLs from a starting base URL, with options to customize the crawl via search query, subdomain inclusion, sitemap handling, and result limits; search effectiveness is site-dependent.

url.description: The starting website URL to map and discover links from. Must be a valid HTTP/HTTPS URL string (e.g., 'https://example.com'). Do NOT pass code snippets, SDK examples, or anything other than a plain URL.

limit.description: Maximum number of links to return. Defaults to 5000. Maximum allowed is 100000.

search.description: Optional search query to guide URL mapping, prioritizing or finding specific page types. 'Smart' search is limited to 1000 initial results in Alpha, but overall mapping can exceed this.

sitemap.description: Sitemap handling mode: 'skip' to exclude sitemaps, 'include' to use sitemaps with other discovery methods (default behavior), or 'only' to return only sitemap URLs.

timeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds. No timeout is applied by default.

location.description: Geographic settings for location-based request processing. Object with 'country' (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, e.g., 'US', 'DE', 'JP') and optionally 'languages' (array of language codes, e.g., ['en'], ['de', 'en']).

ignoreCache.description: If true, bypasses cached sitemap data. Useful when sitemaps have been recently updated. Sitemap data is cached for up to 7 days. Defaults to false.

includeSubdomains.description: If true, includes subdomains of the base URL in the mapping. E.g., if `url` is example.com, blog.example.com is mapped. Defaults to true.

ignoreQueryParameters.description: If true, excludes URLs with query parameters from results. Defaults to true.
